terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Visually estimated from the three-quarter studio view; front and side references provide orthographic proportion checks.

objectClass.notes: Three admitted views describe the same clean stylized game prop. The front view fixes six upper timber bays and two lower door bays; the right-side view fixes wall depth, the solid triangular gable profile, and the sign perpendicular to the facade. The hidden rear continues the observed construction system conservatively. This is an explicit stylized reconstruction, not photoreal or survey/manufacturing geometry.

reasoning: The macro silhouette is a two-storey rectangular hall, one closed gable-roof prism, a chimney, a perpendicular hanging sign, and facade props.
The facade and gable sides require separate stone courses, plaster panels, timber posts, rails, diagonal braces, arcade posts, and two door assemblies.
Identity depends on regular repeated systems: ashlar courses, roof tile rows, chimney bricks, timber bays, door planks, chain links, notice papers, and barrel staves/hoops.
Nine distinct color/material blocks must stay legible without photoreal micro-noise.
Three mutually distinct views reduce occlusion risk, but the rear elevation remains inferred and intentionally conservative.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The simple outer building mass contains a dense, identity-bearing hierarchy. A shallow facade or pair of roof slabs would lose the solid gable, side evidence, timber depth, and prop systems.

detailInventory.note: Twenty observed detail systems are consolidated from the main, front, and side inventories. Every item maps to a component localFeature or material localOverride used by the sculpt spec.

details.description: One continuous closed gable prism creates both roof slopes, the underside, and both triangular end caps.
Regular overlapping terracotta tile rows step down both roof slopes.
A regular capped ridge follows the roof length and remains thicker than tile relief.
The chimney has staggered red brick courses, recessed dark seams, a stone shoulder, and a projecting cap.
Offset rectangular stone blocks create clean recessed mortar lines on front and side walls.
Front timber posts have clean chamfered shafts, stepped collars, broad capitals, and square stone feet.
Six front plaster bays are divided by raised posts, two rails, and alternating diagonal braces.
The right gable uses a central vertical, a collar beam, and mirrored diagonals over the rectangular side bays.
Two double doors are divided into narrow vertical planks by dark recessed seams.
Black strap hinges and circular ring pulls sit proud of both double doors.
Two short gold chain runs suspend the sign from a black projecting arm.
A raised gold inset border follows the clipped shield outline.
Two gold swords with tapered blades, guards, grips, and pommels cross as raised geometry.
Varied parchment sheets overlap across the board with simple ink linework.
Small colored pins and one red wax seal punctuate the paper cluster.
Three bulged wooden barrels use alternating staves and three dark iron hoops.
Timber beams use small clean chamfers that catch broad studio highlights.
Mortar gaps are slightly darker than stone faces without noisy surface grain.
Plaster remains warm ivory with restrained bay-to-bay value variation.
Tile rows alternate among a restrained red-terracotta palette; no random micro-noise is visible.

anatomy.note: Not a character or hybrid subject.

definitionOfDone: The model reads immediately as the same clean stylized fantasy guild from front, side, and three-quarter views.
The building has one closed solid gable-roof prism with a regular relief tile system; two rotated slab roofs are prohibited.
Stone base, front timber arcade, half-timber upper floor, red tile roof, chimney, perpendicular green sword sign, quest board, and three barrels remain separately readable.
The factory returns an action-ready THREE.Group with facade +Z and the lowest visible geometry exactly at y=0.
All materials are MeshStandardMaterial or MeshToonMaterial color blocks with restrained roughness variation and no facade photo, projected photo, or texture billboard.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Share repeated geometries and materials while preserving silhouette, tile rhythm, sign emblem, quest papers, and barrel detail.

lightingFromPhoto: Use a broad warm-neutral key light from upper-front-left at intensity near 2.2 with soft shadows to define roof slopes, chamfers, and timber relief.
Use a low-intensity cool-neutral fill light from rear-right near 0.45 so stone seams and recessed doors remain readable without flattening contrast.
Use a subtle hemisphere or rim/environment light near 0.7 to separate the roof and chimney silhouette from a neutral light-gray studio background.
Use ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure near 1.0 and a soft contact/ground shadow beneath the plinth, quest board, steps, and barrels.
proceduralStrategy: Build one closed indexed triangular-prism roof mesh; never substitute two rotated box slabs.
Build the sole, masonry core, arcade, upper wall, side gables, chimney, doors, sign, board, and barrels as named action-ready groups.
Use shared deterministic repeated geometry for ashlar blocks, timber members, tile rows, bricks, planks, hardware, chains, papers, and barrel parts.
Use solid MeshStandardMaterial color families with restrained value variation and real geometric seams/chamfers; do not project or display reference photos.
Expose door hinge pivots, a sign swing pivot, sockets, primitive collider metadata, and material-boundary destruction groups.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
